1.why: All five screens are static cards with no animation, carousels, modals or pop-ups — only a fixed header, one form card and a log panel.

2.why: Bold dark headings and a single high-contrast primary button dominate each card, though the large black 'Logs (simulated delivery)' panel competes for attention without being important to the user.

3.why: Each screen presents one task with very few elements (one or two fields plus one main button), so the needed action is quick to locate, though there is no progress indicator showing where she is in the flow.

4.why: She must carry a 6-digit code and a long recovery string across screens and satisfy a four-part 14-character password rule, which is a substantial memory/rule load.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced — no masked email echo, no saved account or device recognition; the only pre-filled item is an unrecognisable random recovery string.

7.why: Each card uses one or two short, plain-language sentences in a legible sans-serif at good size and contrast.

8.why: No error message is shown anywhere in the five screenshots — no inline validation text for the email, code, or password-mismatch cases.

9.why: The password rule is stated in words but with no example, and the six-digit code field has no placeholder or sample format; only the pre-filled recovery code implicitly shows a format.

10.why: The single password+code path is clearly labelled ('Recovery code', 'Six-digit verification code'), but no alternative options such as face or biometric login are offered to compare.

11.why: Every screen offers at most two buttons and two fields, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Step 5 confirms 'Accepted securely. Hospital appointment booking may proceed', but most outcomes are only reported in a technical 'SIMULATED …' log panel rather than as clear user-facing confirmation.

13.why: Each card has a one-line instruction plus a repeated 'Stay safe' anti-phishing tip, but there is no task-specific help, tooltip, or guidance for new steps such as where to find the code.

14.why: A 'Start over' button exists on the verification screen, but no back link, resend-code option, or retry affordance appears on the email, password, or privacy screens.

15.why: All five screens reuse the identical header, white rounded card, typography, and dark-blue primary button placement, giving a highly consistent layout.
